The relief team and lounge layout, minutes
It started on time, and an experienced planner led

Attendees were Hugo Nakamura, Caleb Petrov, and the welfare coordinator, along with members of the welcome team and the senior coordinator. The group reviewed routine desk work and confirmed that animal comfort checks remain the first step when a booking is opened. The welfare coordinator reminded the team to note species, temperament, and any signs of stress so that the care plan stays practical and calm. The welcome team was asked to keep guidance short, kind, and easy to follow at check-in, with clear reminders about carrier placement, water access, and quiet handling.

The group also discussed the lounge layout and agreed that the waiting area should support low noise, clear pathways, and enough space for passengers to settle before boarding. Staff noted that simple visual cues help reduce confusion and make it easier to guide travelers with pets through each stage. Loki was mentioned as a useful example of a pet that benefits from a predictable approach and steady reassurance. The meeting also reinforced that staff should speak plainly, avoid rushed instructions, and watch for small changes in behavior that may call for a pause or a brief adjustment to the plan.

The team agreed to keep notes consistent, share updates promptly, and maintain a welcoming tone across the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways. The meeting ended with no further items raised.
